There were several outstanding races at this meeting - the most noteable being the Youth 100y in which John Barnard clocked 10.4,and the Junior 100y/220y where Bob Jones in his first ever try at these distances recorded 10.5/23.5 .

We also did very well on the field with good efforts by John Martin in the Shot,Discus etc.and scored maximum points in the Long Jump which has become a Belgrave parade event - thanks to Dave Ansell -John Mitchell just beating Bob Jones by ½".
Completing the field events picture,Bob Jones jumped within 6" of the Long Jump record with 22'6½" . On the track the best race of the day was undoubtedly the 880 yards.

New junior member Bob Jones showed just how our strength and depth in the field events is growing. He leapt 22'0" to place 2nd in the senior Long Jump and followed this up with a couple of sterling performances in the junior match.

In the 1500m Geoff North sliced a considerable chunk off his best mile time (conversion-wise that is) showing that he is out to give John Thresher a run for his money this season. Bob Jones broke new ground in the Long Jump and is aiming to break 23'0" before long.
Others of the Ansell 'Stable' to do well were Bob Jones (1st in the Junior Triple Jump,4th in the L.Jump and 5th in the furlong) and Cliff Brooks (3rd in the Senior Triple Jump).
Junior Club Records were set by John Mitchell (L.Jump), Jim Vivian (100y), Bob Jones (Triple Jump) and by our relay squad in both sprint relays.

There were very good performances from John Mitchell, who won the Long Jump with 22'7¾", and Bob Jones who was 3rd with 21'0"; both first year seniors and still at the height of arduous winter training schedules.
Nevertheless the Pentathlon was won in grand style by Bob Jones whose best performance was in the Long Jump with 21'7½". This being against the wind on a very cold day.

Bob Jones leapt a windy 22'8½" in the University Champs to place 3rd behind M.Sharpe (Oxford) and Hamish Robertson (Glasgow) who is expected to compete for Scotland in the Commonwealth Games at Trinidad.
It was obvious we were in for an exciting afternoon when with his very first jump in the first event, Bob Jones upped the Champ.Best with a Long Jump of 23'2½".

In the Long Jump, held on Saturday, John Mitchell (best of 23'2½") and Bob Jones (23'5½") were competing and we hoped that the presence of Lynn Davies, R.Stenius, etc. might inspire our duo to something really spectacular.

The Long Jump also produced a close finish with Howell (HHH) winning with 22'8" and Bob Jones and Hudson (TVH) both reaching 22'3½". This time the Belgrave man got the best of the verdict with a superior second best distance.

Another who was well up, until a near fall almost put him out of the race, was Bob Jones. Later, in the four event handicap, Bob produced a massive leap of 22'11½" (from 5" back) and underlined his ability to pull out great Long Jumps no matter what the conditions.

The only pity was that Bob Jones who was within 2" of Derek at the Club Champs was unable to compete due to injury. Beating a classy field, a waterlogged track and stringing together three separate miles of 4:32.8, 4:38.0 and 4:25.0, John Thresher took the first major title of his career .
